text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on March 18 in history.
978 - St Edward the Martyr, King of the English, murdered at Corfe Castle on the orders of his stepmother, eager to see her son Ethelred crowned.
1229 - Roman Emperor Frederick II crowned himself king of Jerusalem during the Sixth Crusade.

1584 - Ivan IV, first to assume the title of Tsar of Russia, died. He inaugurated domestic reforms and conducted successful campaigns against the Tartars, but his cruelty and oppression earned him the nickname Ivan the Terrible.
1662 - The first buses, 8-seater vehicles known as "carrosses a cinq solz", ran in Paris.
1745 - Sir Robert Walpole, British Whig statesman and prime minister, died. He held the first and longest British premiership, from 1721-1742.
1768 - Laurence Sterne, Irish-born clergyman and novelist, author of "The Life and Opinions of Tristram Shandy", died.
1834 - In Dorset, England, six labourers were sentenced to seven years banishment to a penal colony in Australia for forming a trade union. They bacame known as the Tolpuddle Martyrs.
1837 - Grover Cleveland, twice president of the United States from 1885-89 and 1893-97, born.
1842 - Stephane Mallarme, French Symbolist poet, born. Best known for "L'Apres midi d'un faune" which inspired composer Claude Debussy to write an orchestral prelude of the same name.
1844 - Nikolai Rimsky-Korsakov, Russian composer, born. As well as composing and conducting, he was also a teacher and his pupils included Stravinsky and Prokofiev.
1848 - A five-day revolution began in Milan against Austrian rule, forcing governor Joseph Radetzky to withdraw from the city.
1858 - Rudolf Diesel, German engineer and inventor of the engine that bears his name, born.
1869 - Arthur Neville Chamberlain, British Conservative prime minister, born. His premiership covered the period just before World War Two and was marked by his appeasement policy towards Hitler.
1871 - The insurrection of Paris against the French government began. The rebels, known as the Communards, were finally defeated in May.
1893 - Wilfred Owen, English poet, born. He was best-known for his poems about the First World War which expressed his anger and the futility of war.
1905 - Robert Donat, English film actor and Oscar winner for "Goodbye Mr Chips", born.
1913 - King George I of Greece was assassinated at Salonika.
1916 - The Battle of Naroch Lake, an attempt by the Russians to divert German forces from the western front, began.
1921 - Russian soldiers finally put down a rebellion by sailors at Kronstadt, the chief base of the Russian Baltic fleet near Petrograd.
1922 - Mahatma Gandhi was sentenced to six years imprisonment for his civil disobedience campaign.
1932 - John Updike, American novelist, poet and critic, born.
1940 - Hitler and Mussolini met at the Brenner pass in the Alps. It was agreed that Italy would eventually join the war.
1949 - The text of the North Atlantic Treaty was published for the first time.
1965 - Ex-King Farouk I of Egypt died in exile in Italy.
1965 - Soviet cosmonaut Aleksei Leonov made the first space walk.
1967 - The oil tanker Torrey Canyon was wrecked off the Cornish coast of England, spilling 919,000 barrels of oil into the sea.
1970 - Cambodian head of state Prince Norodom Sihanouk was deposed.
1977 - In the Congo, President Marien Ngouabi was assassinated.
1978 - Former Pakistan Prime Minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto was found guilty of ordering the assassination of an opponent and sentenced to death.
1983 - King Umberto II of Italy died in exile in Switzerland.
1990 - Christian Democrats won a landslide victory in the first democratic elections held in East Germany.
1993 - After six days of deadlock, security forces stormed a hijacked Ethiopian airliner in the eastern town of Dire Dawa, killing two of the four hijackers.
1996 - Former Marxist military ruler Mathieu Kerekou won Benin's presidential election run-off against Nicephore Soglo.
